brief: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang resigned after reports he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort; shares fell over 4.3%, pulling the Nasdaq down about 0.4% and pressuring Taiwan and South Korea tech markets. Colette Kress became interim CEO and Harvey C. Jones board chair. UBS draws sector-wide lessons from this: key-person risk and succession planning now matter alongside earnings growth, especially after AI gains concentrated in a narrow group of companies. Separately, US-China chip export restrictions are unlikely to ease and deployment scrutiny could rise, amid reports the White House may push out Commerce Secretary Lutnick over export-control oversight; AI is increasingly geopolitical, raising compliance costs without necessarily denting underlying AI demand, which UBS still calls robust (accelerating cloud revenue, capex forecast at $1.0tr in 2026, $1.4tr in 2027). UBS retains conviction in the structural AI opportunity but favors selectivity, financially strong hyperscalers, and diversification. On rates, UBS flags DXY above 103 (a 10-month high) and 2-year yields up 35bp this week to 4.89% on hawkish Fed commentary; it sees at least two more hikes, favors short/medium bonds, and expects the dollar supported near term but turns bearish on USD further ahead.
